name: North Dakota

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).
Motor fuel is exempt from the general sales tax (per-gallon excise instead).
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
gaps: Some North Dakota cities cap their tax on a single large purchase (for example the first $2,500 or so); caps are not modeled, which matters little for everyday store sales.
2 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; a tract at least half in such a city takes the rate of its own county part.
1 town or township that is not a Census place has its rate listed here, matched to tracts through Census county subdivisions; it adds a local rate to the county's.

programs: Renaissance Zones are mapped for Fargo (the city's layer of zone blocks, edited January 2025, after its 2024 plan update) and Bismarck (the city's block layer, June 2024, without the blocks it marks complete). The Department of Commerce approves each city's zone; it counted 58 cities with one in June 2020. West Fargo's isn't mapped: its only layer dates from 2017, and the city applied in 2025 to extend its zone for ten years (Cass County's letter of support, May 19, 2025), with the outcome not confirmed. Other cities' zones aren't mapped.
